36 A circuit consists of a battery, a high-resistance voltmeter and four fixed resistors, as shown. The
battery has an electromotive force (e.m.f.) of 15.0 V and negligible internal resistance.
15.0 V
24.0 
6.0 
V
6.0 

What is the reading on the voltmeter?
A
3.0 V
B
6.0 V
C
9.0 V
D
12.0 V

hints: Notice the voltmeter joins the midpoint of the upper $24.0 \text{ } \Omega$ and $6.0 \text{ } \Omega$ branch to the midpoint of the lower $6.0 \text{ } \Omega$ and $9.0 \text{ } \Omega$ branch, with $15.0 \text{ V}$ across both branches.

Treat each branch as a separate potential divider and work out how the $15.0 \text{ V}$ splits in proportion to resistance in the upper $30.0 \text{ } \Omega$ branch and in the lower $15.0 \text{ } \Omega$ branch.
Find the potential of each middle node measured from the same battery terminal, then subtract the two potentials to get what the voltmeter between them reads.
walkthrough: Set a reference: let the right-hand common node be $0 \text{ V}$, so the left-hand common node is at $15.0 \text{ V}$ because e.m.f. is $15.0 \text{ V}$ with negligible internal resistance.
Upper branch: total resistance is $24.0 + 6.0 = 30.0 \text{ } \Omega$, so current is $I_{top} = V/R = 15.0/30.0 = 0.50 \text{ A}$.

Voltage drop from the left node to the upper midpoint across $24.0 \text{ } \Omega$ is $I_{top} \times 24.0 = 0.50 \times 24.0 = 12.0 \text{ V}$, so upper midpoint potential is $15.0 - 12.0 = 3.0 \text{ V}$.
Lower branch: total resistance is $6.0 + 9.0 = 15.0 \text{ } \Omega$, so current is $I_{bot} = 15.0/15.0 = 1.0 \text{ A}$.
Voltage drop from the left node to the lower midpoint across $6.0 \text{ } \Omega$ is $1.0 \times 6.0 = 6.0 \text{ V}$, so lower midpoint potential is $15.0 - 6.0 = 9.0 \text{ V}$.
The high-resistance voltmeter draws negligible current, so it reads the difference: $|9.0 - 3.0| = 6.0 \text{ V}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: 3.0 V is the potential of only the upper middle node relative to one end, not the difference between the two middle nodes measured by the voltmeter.

B.explanation: The upper middle node is at 3.0 V and the lower middle node is at 9.0 V relative to the same end, so the potential difference is $9.0 - 3.0 = 6.0 \text{ V}$.

C.explanation: 9.0 V is the potential of only the lower middle node relative to one end, not the difference between the upper and lower middle nodes.

D.explanation: 12.0 V is the voltage drop across the $24.0 \text{ } \Omega$ resistor alone, not the voltage between the two divider midpoints.
